headline: MGS edge lower in quiet trade; belly leads as 5Y benchmark slips 2bp to 3.61%
summary: Malaysian government bonds firmed slightly on Tuesday: BNM's benchmark closes showed the 5Y MGS 2bp lower at 3.61% and the 10Y 1bp lower at 3.84%, and FAST's dealer curve eased by about 1bp from 5 to 15 years. Trading stayed light ahead of Nvidia's results and the Fed minutes, with the ringgit steady near 4.09 per dollar. GII tracked MGS, the 10Y GII closing 1bp lower at 3.88%.
drivers: FAST's MGS curve fell 0.6–0.9bp from 5 to 15 years (5Y 3.636%, 10Y 3.854%) while the 1Y and 3Y were unchanged. Benchmark volumes were modest, led by the 3Y MGS (RM301m) and the 10Y GII (RM472m).
Last week's RM3.5bn reopening of the 15Y GII 7/40 cleared at an average 4.158% with a 2.32x bid-to-cover, about 26bp above its June sale; the 15Y MGS sits at 4.15% on the FAST curve.
BNM kept the OPR at 2.75% on Nov 5 with a slightly more hawkish tone, so the front end trades well above the policy rate: the 3Y MGS is about 67bp over the OPR.
US Treasuries rallied overnight as tech stocks slid before Nvidia's results, which helped local duration at the margin; USD/MYR held near 4.09–4.10.
data: Weaker demand and a higher clearing yield than earlier sales show investors want more term premium for long ringgit duration.
A firmer tone opens the door to a hike next year; that keeps the front end and belly from rallying far.
view: MGS are range-bound and lean slightly firmer while Treasuries rally, but the long end needs better auction demand before it can outperform. Prefer the 5–7Y belly over 15–20Y; stay neutral on the front end while the market weighs a 2027 OPR hike.

buckets.name: Front end 3Y vs OPR
buckets.why: The 3Y MGS is 3.422% on the FAST curve, about 67bp over the 2.75% OPR, which already prices some chance of a hike in 2027. The 3Y benchmark closed flat at 3.41%.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add only if the 3Y backs up toward 3.55% without a change in BNM's tone.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y
buckets.why: The 5Y fell 0.9bp to 3.636% on FAST and the benchmark closed 2bp lower at 3.61%. It carries well over the OPR with less supply risk than the long end.
buckets.call: Hold a small overweight; take profit near 3.55%, cut above 3.72%.

buckets.name: Long end 10s30s
buckets.why: The 30Y sits at 4.331%, about 48bp over the 10Y. Recent long-dated GII sales cleared well above earlier levels, so dealers keep a supply premium in the long end.
buckets.call: Neutral until a long auction draws a stronger bid; then favour flatteners.

buckets.name: GII vs MGS 10Y
buckets.why: The 10Y GII is 3.892% against 3.854% for MGS, a gap of under 4bp, tight for GII's usual liquidity premium.
buckets.call: Prefer MGS over GII at 10Y while the gap is below about 5bp.

buckets.name: AAA credit 5Y
buckets.why: FAST's AAA 5Y curve is 4.114%, about 48bp over the 5Y MGS.
buckets.call: Neutral; add AAA paper only if the spread widens past about 55bp.

watch: Next: Treasuries after Nvidia's results and the Fed minutes, the ringgit, BNM's next auction announcement and month-end flows.
